content.text:
I traced the history of the `mon_host=...\\:` escape sequence in `KVMPhysicalDisk.java` from the fix commit all the way back through every commit that touched this line (renames, refactors, condition changes), and the double-backslash literal `"\\\\:"` was present unchanged from the very first commit that introduced `RBDStringBuilder` in 2012 through to the fix in 2021 — no intermediate commit ever modified this specific string literal.

## Bug-Introducing Commits
BIC: 258a269d1dd1e7932d9f9d43c2dfd6be4c3cf944

## Reasoning

**(1) Investigation:** Starting from the fix diff (which changes `"\\\\:"` → `"\\:"` in the Java string literal that builds an RBD connection string), I walked the file's git history (`git log -p` on the current path, then on the renamed/older path, then via glob to bridge the rename) to find every commit that ever touched that line.

**(2) What introduced the bug:** Commit `258a269d1dd7...` (Edison Su, 2012-07-30) added `plugins/hypervisors/kvm/src/com/cloud/hypervisor/kvm/storage/KVMPhysicalDisk.java` for the first time, including:
```java
rbdOpts += ":mon_host=" + monHost + "\\\\:" + monPort;
```
In a Java source string, `"\\\\:"` decodes to the two-character sequence `\\:` (double backslash + colon) at runtime, when the RBD connection string format only expects a single escaped backslash (`\:`). This double-escaping bug was baked in at creation.

**(3) Supporting evidence:** I confirmed every subsequent commit touching this code (`471915cbc5` in refactoring the mon_host/port logic, `60e16792a5` changing the method signature, `bd367e1469` renaming the file to the Maven `src/main/java` layout, `b8c4be7638` changing the `monPort` condition from `!= 6789` to `> 0`) all carried forward the identical `"\\\\:"` literal verbatim — none of them altered the escaping. Only the final fix commit `ba5f390d50` (2021-01-05) corrects it to `"\\:"`. Since the erroneous escaping was never modified between 2012 and the fix, the defect traces back to its origin at commit `258a269d1d`.

I'm fairly confident in this conclusion since the string literal is a small, distinct piece of code whose history I could trace completely and unambiguously — there's no ambiguity about which commit changed it last before the fix (none did, until the fix itself).
